rationale:
Evidence. Iteration 1 (narrow 15 mm array, base_speed 1.3, kp 2.5, kd 0.3) is still the best raced design at 178.2. It finished 3 of 20 oval runs at about 1.97 s, but it averaged 1.25 to 1.9 line-loss events per run and max_error about 0.061 to 0.063 m, right at the 0.06 m off-track limit. Iteration 2 showed that widening the array to 22.5 mm spacing does not help line retention (line_loss stayed at 1.0, score 81.1), so the narrow layout stays. Iteration 3 (kp 2.2, kd 0.25) dropped to 106.7 with the same line-loss pattern. Its oscillation fell to 0.14 on the oval, so lower kd did not cure the line loss, and the kp/kd change cannot be separated from the score drop.

Review note. The Evaluator's review of the iteration 3 candidate gave kp as both 2.5 and 2.2. The candidate's controller field is kp 2.2, so I treat 2.2 as the value that was raced and the value that was approved. Here I return to kp 2.5 explicitly, so the intended kp is unambiguous.

Change. I keep the iteration 1 geometry and gains (kp 2.5, kd 0.3, ki 0, sensor_weights [2,1,0,-1,-2], last_direction) and lower base_speed from 1.3 to 1.1. This is a single-variable test against the best raced design. The Evaluator's stated next step applies because line_loss_events are still 1 or more and max_error is near 0.06. Each line-loss event costs 15 points per unit progress, so keeping the line matters more than a small time gain.

Expected result. line_loss_events fall toward 0 to 0.5 and max_error drops below about 0.055, which allows more oval and s-bend finishes. Completion time rises to roughly 2.2 to 2.5 s on the oval, which is still under the 3.0 s limit. Oscillation may stay near 0.3 on the oval because kd is unchanged; if it does, the next step is kd 0.25 or kp 2.0.

Hypotheses to test next. (a) Speed in the bends, not sensor coverage, drives the line loss, so lowering speed should cut line_loss_events. (b) If line loss is still above 0.5 at 1.1, the limit is the gain/geometry combination rather than speed alone.
